text:
marta: Filing a docs PR after a customer hit a installer edge-case on air-gapped RHEL7/RHEL8 minimal images: restorecon isn't present and the installer tried to run it during preflight which caused the installer to bail. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4791

devon: can you paste the install log snippet so we know the exact failure mode?

marta: sure — short extract: `preflight: running /sbin/restorecon -R /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket` -> `restorecon: SELinux: Could not locate policy file` -> installer exits non-zero. This happens on minimal images with policycoreutils missing.

packaging: packaging note — we can and should ship a small .fc (filecontexts) fragment in the RPM and call `rpm --restorecon` as part of post-install. That avoids dependence on semanage/restorecon at install time and works in air-gapped environments. I'll add a sample .fc in the PR.

devon: good. for customers who can't change packaging we should document two supported installer behaviours: 1) Installer uses packaged .fc and runs rpm --restorecon (recommended); 2) Installer falls back to creating the dir and `chcon -t var_run_t` on minimal systems and emits a note that this is not persistent across SELinux relabels.

marta: added both options in the PR. also included a tiny `postinstall.sh` example that tries rpm --restorecon first, then restorecon, then chcon as last resort (keeps reliance on coreutils/systemctl only). snippet in PR: ```bash
# postinstall snippet
FC_PKG=/usr/lib/sysusers.d/redwood-hsm.fc
if rpm -q redwood-docs >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  rpm --restorecon -a || true
fi
if command -v restorecon >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  /sbin/restorecon -R /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket || true
else
  chcon -t var_run_t /var/lib/redwood/hsm-socket || true
fi
```

packaging: small FYI: prefer `var_run_t` or `redwood_var_t` depending on our packaged policy. I'll add both examples in Advanced > SELinux Packaging. Also include the `.fc` sample that sets `var_run_t` for the socket path.

docs-bot: Link-check: PR 4791 flagged an internal KB link `https://kb.redwood.internal/selinux-packaging` 404. Please remove or point to canonical internal KB.

security: please ensure the docs do not advise `setenforce 0`. Also, avoid recommending system-wide SELinux disable. Add explicit "do not disable SELinux" note in Troubleshooting.

devon: done — PR now has a short Troubleshooting bullet: "Do not disable SELinux system-wide (for example `setenforce 0`). Use the chcon fallback only if you cannot run semanage/restorecon during install; plan to apply semanage fcontext permanently when feasible."

marta: added an appendix with an RPM `.fc` example and `systemd-tmpfiles.d` alternative: we can also populate `/run/redwood/hsm` at boot with tmpfiles.d to avoid needing installer actions on some systems. snippet: `d /run/redwood/hsm 0755 redwood redwood -`

packaging: can we add a small test in the packaging CI that simulates a minimal container without policycoreutils and verifies installer falls back to chcon and the service starts? I'll add that as a follow-up.

docs-bot: CI lint: PR 4791 passes markdown checks after removing broken internal link. Manual approval required for internal KB links.

marta: great — I'll ask for security sign-off and then request merge. Leaving thread open for any packaging/test follow-ups.
